strengths: Novel problem formulation: Using 4D semantic occupancy as intermediate representation for robot video generation is intuitive and well-motivated, providing finer-grained geometric and semantic guidance than high-level action sequences alone

Comprehensive system design: Presents end-to-end framework including practical dataset curation pipeline, video generation architecture, and two extensions (multiview and sim-to-real), demonstrating good systems thinking

Thorough experimental validation: Evaluation on three major robot datasets with multiple complementary metrics (PSNR, SSIM, FID, FVDL), comprehensive ablation studies (Tables 3-4) isolating component contributions, and demonstration of generalization across datasets

Excellent supplementary materials: 11 pages providing extensive implementation details including dataset statistics, architecture specifications, hyperparameter tables, and additional ablations that enhance reproducibility
Strong qualitative results: Generated videos demonstrate visually plausible manipulation sequences with good cross-view consistency despite acknowledged limitations
Practical relevance: Addresses real challenges in robot learning including limited high-quality simulation data and sim-to-real transfer gaps
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core contribution is primarily architectural/combinatorial (pretrained CogVideoX-2b + standard MonoSLAM + Gaussian rendering + existing VLM semantic labeling) rather than novel algorithmic or mathematical contributions

Modest quantitative improvements: Performance gains are often marginal (<1 PSNR point on several datasets; RT-1 baseline even outperforms on PSNR); while FID improvements are more significant, standard metrics correlate poorly with perceptual quality in action-conditioned videos

Incomplete validation of key claims: Multiview generation extension acknowledges 'noticeable artifacts and empty regions' yet lacks quantitative cross-view consistency metrics; sim-to-real transfer (ORV-S2R) presented as contribution but validated with only one qualitative example and no downstream task evaluation

Dataset curation scalability concerns: Pipeline requires semantic labeling, dense 3D reconstruction, and dataset-specific hyperparameter tuning (σ=3.7); reprocesses existing datasets but does not demonstrate applicability to entirely new environments or robot morphologies

Insufficient failure analysis: Section G (Limitations) is too brief with only end-effector pose limitation discussed; no systematic analysis of failure modes, no negative examples shown, and no exploration of scenarios where occupancy representation is insufficient

Lack of theoretical grounding: Why occupancy over alternatives? No principled comparison with 3D keypoints, scene graphs, or other world models; choice appears empirically validated but theoretically unmotivated

Evaluation limitations: No human studies validating perceptual quality improvements; high FID values (28-42 range) suggest significant domain gap persists; no downstream evaluation of whether generated videos actually improve robot policy learning; missing diversity/mode collapse analysis
Missing practical analysis: No inference time measurements, memory requirements, or computational cost comparisons relative to baselines; unclear if real-time generation is feasible
Action conditioning under-explored: Limited analysis of sensitivity to action noise, out-of-distribution actions, or action representation choices; no systematic ablation on action embedding design

Reproducibility gaps: No code release mentioned, Gaussian rendering hyperparameter choices lack justification, VLM prompts for semantic labeling not provided, insufficient detail on dataset preprocessing procedures

strengths: Novel occupancy-centric framework providing an effective intermediate representation between action sequences and pixel-space videos, offering geometric and semantic guidance
Comprehensive system design with three variants (base, multi-view, sim-to-real) demonstrating framework versatility
Valuable curated dataset contribution creating semantic occupancy labels for existing robot manipulation benchmarks (BridgeV2, Droid, RT-1) with detailed curation documentation
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 3-4) systematically validating different components and their individual contributions
Extensive implementation details in supplementary materials including hyperparameters, training procedures, and computational requirements supporting reproducibility
Experiments across three datasets with reasonable visual quality results and multi-view generation capabilities
weaknesses: Mixed quantitative results: ORV does not consistently outperform baselines (Table 2 shows IRASim achieving better metrics on BridgeV2), without clear explanation of when occupancy provides advantages
Critical absence of downstream evaluation: No assessment of whether generated videos improve robot policy learning or any human studies validating semantic correctness and visual quality

Insufficient justification for occupancy representation: No empirical demonstration that occupancy is superior to simpler alternatives like direct RGB conditioning with actions or other 3D representations
Data curation scalability concerns: Manual semantic labeling and per-dataset engineering required; 8TB disk space; unclear generalization to new domains; limited pseudo-label quality validation

ORV-MV multi-view design limitation: Requires first-frame multi-view observations at test time, severely restricting practical applicability to systems with single cameras; acknowledged geometric inconsistencies persist
Limited baseline comparisons: Missing recent controllable video generation methods; ControlNet comparison dismissed without fair comparison; some baselines underperform unexpectedly
Narrow generalization scope: Evaluation limited to tabletop manipulation with similar datasets; no experiments on other robot types, morphologies, or complex manipulation scenarios
Incomplete occupancy representation: Captures only end-effector pose not full articulated joint information; sparse grids may lose fine-grained interaction details critical for manipulation
Metric limitations: Standard PSNR/SSIM/FID/FVDL metrics do not directly measure semantic correctness or control precision; lacks task-specific evaluation metrics

Presentation density: Occupancy-centric design intuition could be clearer; some notation inconsistently applied; design choice ablations missing (e.g., occupancy resolution, why occupancy over alternatives)
